data.title: China advances a step toward dissolving China Evergrande
data.description:
A Chinese court accepted on Friday a bankruptcy liquidation case against China Evergrande's (EGRNF) mainland Chinese property development subsidiary, according to media reports.

The development came a day after a court in the city of Shenzhen sentenced Hui Kan Yan, the company's founder, to life in prison for financial crimes.

A court in China's Guangzhou accepted the liquidation case of Hengda Real Estate Group,  Reuters reported.

The move suggests that the Chinese government may "have a road map" for concluding the Evergrande (EGRNF) saga, Foreky Wong, a founding partner at Fortune Ark Restructuring and a restructuring specialist, told the Associated Press.

“They will need to do these (steps) sooner or later,” he said. However, “Evergrande is such a big company. Its bankruptcy proceedings will last for a while.”

The property development giant defaulted on more than $300B of debt in 2021.

Evergrande's holding company was listed in Hong Kong, but most of its operations were in China. With the company subject to two different legal systems, it may be difficult for the Hong Kong court-appointed liquidators to claw back any assets that are recovered in China, the AP said.

data.title: Biggest stock movers Friday: ROST, MSTR, MRVL, HOOD, and more
data.description:
Stock futures edged slightly higher on Friday as markets attempted to rebound from Thursday's steep selloff. Gains were supported by a pullback in U.S. Treasury yields, though sentiment remained cautious with Brent crude hovering near $93 a barrel and lingering policy uncertainty following hawkish signals from Fed meeting minutes.

Here are some of Friday's biggest stock movers:

Biggest stock gainers

  • TG Therapeutics (TGTX) +12% - Shares jumped amid renewed takeover speculation after traders cited a Betaville “uncooked” alert suggesting the company may have attracted interest from an unnamed U.S.-listed biopharma with a $20B-$40B market capitalization.
  • Robinhood Markets (HOOD) +12% - Crypto-linked stocks rose as Bitcoin (BTC-USD) rebounded to around $77K, swinging between $72.9K and $79.4K during the day and putting it on track for its strongest weekly gain in more than two years after falling below $64K earlier this week. The rally has been fueled by falling Treasury yields, renewed optimism around U.S. crypto regulation, and a major short squeeze that liquidated roughly $2.7B in crypto short positions, lifting crypto-linked stocks including Coinbase Global (COIN) +8%, Circle Internet Group (CRCL) +6%, and Bitdeer Technologies (BTDR) +4%.
  • Strategy (MSTR) +7% - Shares rallied after the firm returned to profitability on its Bitcoin holdings, swinging to an estimated $1.4B unrealized gain as the cryptocurrency surged nearly 22% over five sessions to around $78,500. The turnaround follows a deep drawdown that saw unrealized losses top $13B when Bitcoin hit $58,000 in July.
  • Ross Stores (ROST) +3% - Shares surged after the retailer reported a stronger-than-expected quarter, with sales up 14% to $6.3B, comparable store sales up 10%, and EPS of $2.66, helped by a $253M IEEPA tariff refund. Ross raised its FY2026 EPS outlook to $8.61-$8.77 from $7.50-$7.74 and increased its planned 2026 store openings to 115.

Biggest stock losers

  • OSI Systems (OSIS) -8% - Shares plunged after Q4 revenue declined 4.1% Y/Y to $484.1M, missing estimates by $45.6M, despite non-GAAP EPS of $3.78 narrowly beating expectations. FY2027 revenue guidance of $1.875B-$1.93B came in below the $1.94B consensus, while EPS guidance of $11.13-$11.49 was broadly in line. The company also expanded its buyback authorization by 1M shares, leaving 1.08M shares available for repurchase.
  • Marvell Technology (MRVL) -6% - Shares fell despite its expanded partnership with Google ((GOOG)) to develop custom AI chips, as investors appeared to look past the deal following this week’s initial rally. Wedbush said the agreement reinforces the advantage of companies with custom-silicon design capabilities, with Marvell’s partnership spanning AI inference accelerators, storage and network controllers, and near-memory compute.
  • Flowers Foods (FLO) -5% - Shares fell after Q2 revenue declined 4% Y/Y to $1.19B, missing estimates by $40M, while non-GAAP EPS of $0.21 also came in below expectations. The company cut its FY2026 outlook, now expecting $5.07B-$5.14B in sales and $0.75-$0.85 in adjusted EPS, below the consensus of $5.17B and $0.83, respectively.

data.title: Citadel shed more than 80% of aggregate risk from Situational Awareness portfolio - CNBC
data.description:
Ken Griffin's Citadel sold more than 80% of the aggregate risk from the original Situational Awareness portfolio, the artificial-intelligence-focused hedge fund founded by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner.

The hedge fund completed nearly 100 block trades totaling over $4 billion in market value, CNBC reported, citing a letter the hedge fund sent to investors.

"These included the largest intraday block trades of the year in 10 different names," Griffin commented in the letter. "In the United States we quickly exited the vast majority of the Vega risk, saving substantial capital in the process. Of the remaining positions in G10, only five have a gross market value greater than $250 million."

Citadel's multi-strategy fund finished up July 5.94%, bringing year-to-date performance to 12%.

Situational had reportedly held urgent talks with multiple investors about selling assets or raising fresh capital before focusing on a transaction with a single large buyer to accelerate the process and limit further losses.

Founded roughly two years ago, Situational Awareness had amassed more than $20 billion in assets under management, according to the Financial Times.

data.title: Apollo discloses 'social engineering incident' potentially impacting personal information security
data.description:
Apollo Global Management (APO) wrote to the California attorney general about a recent "social engineering incident" that may impact the security of some personal information.

The alternative asset management found in an investigation that there was unauthorized access to certain cloud platforms between July 6 and July 10. 

"During our investigation, we learned on August 12, 2026, that the information potentially impacted by this incident included your name, date of birth, contact information, home address, and your Social Security Number," said the letter to Rob Bonta.

"We have no evidence that your information has been publicly posted or used for identity theft or fraud at this time," said the letter.

"We take the confidentiality of the data entrusted to us very seriously and are therefore offering complimentary third-party identity protection and credit monitoring services," said the letter.

data.title: Nvidia, Micron among 10 stocks initiated with bullish views at BMO Capital
data.description:
BMO Capital began coverage of 12 semiconductor and quantum computing stocks, including Nvidia (NVDA), Micron Technology (MU), and D-Wave Quantum (QBTS).

The analysts initiated 10 stocks with an Outperform rating and two with Market Perform ratings.

"We're initiating coverage of Semiconductors and Quantum Computing with a positive outlook. We're bullish on 1) AI; and 2) Analog sectors. AI demand remains strong driven by DC infrastructure deployments and insatiable demand for AI tokens. CSP/hyperscaler and AI lab capex remain elevated in a race to reach AGI. We see AI in the early innings with many years of capex growth to support token demand (+6,050% growth) and tokenomics. We're optimistic on early-cycle recovery of analog companies. Analog upcycle is led by industrial auto is starting to pick up, while geo landscape remains positive for defense," said analysts led by Harsh Kumar.

The analysts noted that their top AI pick is Nvidia as the de facto leader with full-stack hardware/software and market share dominance. They also see Broadcom (AVGO), Micron, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Marvell Technology (MRVL), and Semtech (SMTC) well positioned in data center, or DC/AI buildouts. Analog names the analysts favor are Analog Devices (ADI), Impinj (PI), and Microchip Technology (MCHP).

Nvidia

The analysts began coverage of Nvidia with an Outperform rating and a $340 price target, noting that the stock is their top large-cap pick.

"Nvidia is our top pick as the industry's lead AI supplier. NVDA's GPU started the AI revolution and the company is now proving fully integrated AI system (NVL72) of hardware and software for compute. Demand robust for the next 12 months," said Kumar and his team.

Broadcom

Broadcom was initiated with an Outperform rating and $455 price target. The analysts noted that Broadcom is the industry leader in custom ASIC ((XPU)) and Ethernet networking. The company is working with nearly all major hyperscalers and AI labs developing XPUs, adding that visibility is strong for the next two years.

Micron

The analysts started coverage of Micron with a $1,300 price target and Outperform rating.

"Micron is a memory supplier benefiting from the AI memory supercycle. AI demand for HBM [high-bandwidth memory] continues to remain strong. Supply/demand tight leading to DRAM/NAND price increases. LTA/SCA [Long-Term Agreements/Strategic Customer Agreements] creates visibility," said the analysts.

AMD

Kumar and his team began coverage of AMD with an Outperform rating and $550 price target. AMD is second behind Nvidia in providing a complete AI system. Helios is starting to ramp up in the second half of 2026. Multi-year deals, secured with Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic for Helios racks into 2030, the analysts added.

Marvell

BMO initiated coverage of Marvell with a $250 price target and an Outperform rating. The analysts noted that Marvell is a leading DC infrastructure supplier. The company is a leader in PAM4 optical connectivity. Networking portfolio supports scale up, out, and across. The company is emerging as a key supplier in XPU and XPU-attach, according to the analysts.

Semtech

Semtech was initiated with a $155 price target and an Outperform rating. "Semtech is a niche semiconductor supplier. Growth led by optical DC modules. Revenues expected to step up from LPO/ACC [Linear Pluggable Optics/Active Copper Cable] connectivity. Sustained steady 15-20% growth from LoRa," said Kumar and his team.

Analog Devices

The analysts started coverage with an Outperform rating and a $430 price target. The analysts noted that Analog Devices is a well-managed company positioned for the broader semiconductor cycle upturn. Revenues are 75% industrial/auto markets, and demand signals are improving. In addition, customer orders are increasing, and backlog is starting to grow. 

Impinj

The analysts said Impinj is the leader in RFID with an estimated 65% share of the global market. Channel inventory is cleared. Total Addressable Market, or TAM, is increasing as use cases are expanding into general merchandising in the food/meat category, the analysts added. The stock was initiated with an Outperform rating and a $220 price target.

Microchip Technology 

BMO began coverage with an Outperform rating and a $95 price target. The analysts said that Microchip benefits from improving semi-cycles and favorable macro conditions. Industrial is in full swing while auto is showing early recovery. Improved utilization rates help drive margins higher, the analysts added.

D-Wave

"In quantum computing, we initiate DWave with OP rating as we see best fit for commercial success, considering its presence in two leading quantum approaches. The quantum computing industry is still in its early days, and we see it as a long-term growth story," said Kumar and his team. The stock was initiated with an Outperform rating and a $35 price target.

Macom Technology (MTSI) and Skyworks Solutions (SWKS) were initiated with Market Perform ratings, with price targets of $355 and $70, respectively.

data.title: Walmart rolling out Tap to Pay for contactless check-out
data.description:
• Walmart (WMT) is adding a contactless payment system, including Apple Pay, at select stores and Sam’s Club locations beginning August 24, with a further expansion planned for later this year.
  • Tap to Pay at Walmart (WMT) will allow shoppers to hold a credit card, phone, or smartwatch near a card reader to send payment data instantly without swiping or inserting a credit or debit card. Customers can also add eligible Walmart, Sam’s Club, and OnePay cards to their digital wallets. 
  • While other retailers embraced Apple Pay for contactless checkout, Walmart (WMT) opted to stick with its own QR code-based system, Walmart Pay, despite consumers’ preference for Apple Pay.
  • Despite welcome news for a large contingent of Walmart shoppers, the news failed to put a dent in the negative price action for the stock following disappointing second-quarter results.

data.title: Prospect Capital outlines AI initiatives targeting tens of millions in annualized cash flow benefit
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Prospect Capital Corporation (PSEC) Q4 2026

Management View

  • John Barry (Chairman of the Board & CEO) highlighted stable earnings power and balance sheet positioning, stating, "In the June quarter, our net investment income, or NII, was $78 million, consistent with the prior quarter or $0.15 per common share." He added, "Our NAV was approximately $2.9 billion or $5.71 per common share" and noted leverage, "At June 30, our net debt to total assets ratio was 28.6%."
  • John Barry (Chairman of the Board & CEO) announced updated payouts, saying, "We are announcing monthly common shareholder distributions of $0.035 per share for each of September and October." He also framed the longer-term distribution record: "Since our IPO 22 years ago through our October 2026 declared distribution, we will have distributed over $4.8 billion or $22.14 per share."
  • John Barry (Chairman of the Board & CEO) emphasized a realized exit outcome, stating, "On July 1, 2026, Prospect closed a successful sale of its portfolio company, Valley Electric, with total consideration of approximately $328 million." He added that Prospect "achieved a 20.5% realized gross annualized IRR and 4.8x multiple of invested capital" on the investment.
  • Michael Eliasek (President & COO) underscored portfolio mix and origination focus: "We primarily focus on senior and secured debt, which was 84% of our portfolio at cost as of June" and "Middle market lending comprised 91% of our originations during the June quarter with a continued focus on first lien senior secured loans." He also said, "We've essentially completed the exit of our subordinated structured notes portfolio as of June with such portfolio representing around 0% of our investment portfolio at cost."
  • Kristin Van Dask (CFO, Treasurer, Secretary & Chief Compliance Officer) emphasized liquidity and funding, stating, "Our combined balance sheet cash and undrawn revolving credit facility commitments stood at $1.6 billion as of June prior to the sale of Valley Electric on July 1." She added, "We held $4.2 billion of our assets as unencumbered assets, representing approximately 66% of our portfolio" and said, "At June 30, 2026, our weighted average cost of unsecured debt financing was 4.78%."

Outlook

  • John Barry (Chairman of the Board & CEO) did not provide formal earnings guidance in the prepared remarks and instead focused on operational initiatives, stating, "We continue to see many opportunities to deploy large language models, generative, predictive, machine learning and other AI and automation tools across every one of Prospect's businesses and investment portfolios." He added, "We believe these initiatives will capture economic upside from profit enhancements, both in terms of revenues and costs and may result in tens of millions of dollars of annualized cash flow benefit."
  • Michael Eliasek (President & COO) outlined capital redeployment priorities tied to real estate exits, stating, "We expect to continue to redeploy future real estate property exit proceeds primarily into more first lien senior secured corporate loans with selected equity-linked investments."

Financial Results

  • John Barry (Chairman of the Board & CEO) reported funding mix and asset coverage, stating, "Unsecured debt plus unsecured perpetual preferred was 83.7% of total debt plus preferred" and, separately, "At June 30, our net debt to total assets ratio was 28.6%."
  • Michael Eliasek (President & COO) provided portfolio and credit datapoints, stating, "As of June 2026, we held 91 portfolio companies across 31 different industries with an aggregate fair value of $6.3 billion" and "Nonaccruals as a percentage of total assets as of June stood at approximately 0.7% based on fair market value, consistent with the prior quarter." He also said, "Payment-in-kind interest income... was 10% of total investment income for the June 2026 fiscal year."
  • Kristin Van Dask (CFO, Treasurer, Secretary & Chief Compliance Officer) detailed commitments and revolver terms, stating, "We currently have $2.12 billion of commitments from 48 banks" and "The facility does not mature until June 2029 and revolves until June 2028. Our drawn pricing continues to be SOFR plus 2.05%."

Q&A

  • No analyst Q&A session was included in this transcript, as the operator stated, "At this time, there are no further questions."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analyst sentiment: No analyst questions were asked in the current quarter call, limiting direct read-through on investor concerns; in both quarters, the operator ended Q&A without questions (current: "there are no further questions"; prior: "This concludes our question-and-answer session").
  • Management sentiment: Management’s tone in prepared remarks was slightly positive and opportunity-focused, with John Barry (Chairman of the Board & CEO) saying, "We view artificial intelligence as a transformational once-in-a-generation opportunity to enhance profitability" and "We intend Prospect to be the leader applying transformative AI tools to all we do."
  • Current vs. previous quarter: The current call leaned more heavily into AI as a value driver ("may result in tens of millions of dollars of annualized cash flow benefit"), while the prior quarter framed AI as one component within a broader list of strategic priorities ("adoption of artificial intelligence and automation initiatives focused on enhancing revenues and reducing costs").

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • John Barry (Chairman of the Board & CEO) reported NII as "consistent with the prior quarter" in the June quarter, while also reporting a lower NAV per share versus the March quarter (June: "$5.71" vs. March: "$6.05").
  • Portfolio commentary was broadly consistent, with Michael Eliasek (President & COO) continuing to stress first-lien middle-market lending and low software exposure (June: "2.3%"; March: "2.5%"), while the current quarter added a major realized exit announcement ("sale of... Valley Electric").
  • Distribution messaging narrowed in the current call to two months ("September and October") versus four months in the prior call ("May, June, July and August"), while both reiterated long-term cumulative distributions around "$4.8 billion."

Risks and Concerns

  • Michael Eliasek (President & COO) flagged ongoing credit monitoring areas via reported indicators, stating, "Nonaccruals... stood at approximately 0.7%" and that payment-in-kind income was "10% of total investment income" for the fiscal year.
  • Kristin Van Dask (CFO, Treasurer, Secretary & Chief Compliance Officer) outlined exposure to future funding needs and commitments, stating, "Our unfunded eligible commitments to portfolio companies totaled approximately $65 million" and noting that "$52 million are considered at our sole discretion."
  • John Barry (Chairman of the Board & CEO) pointed to post-close leverage implications around the Valley Electric proceeds and revolver usage, stating, "If the cash received on July 1... had been received previously and repaid borrowings under our revolver, the revolver's drawn amount would have been $323 million on June 30 on a pro forma basis."

Final Takeaway

Prospect’s management emphasized stable quarter-to-quarter net investment income, declared continued monthly common distributions at $0.035 for September and October, and highlighted the July 1 Valley Electric exit (approximately $328 million consideration) with a reported 20.5% realized gross annualized IRR and 4.8x multiple. Leadership repeatedly framed AI and automation as a profitability lever, explicitly stating an expectation for “tens of millions of dollars of annualized cash flow benefit,” while continuing to describe a portfolio rotation toward first-lien senior secured middle-market loans and redeployment of real estate exit proceeds into corporate lending.

data.title: Cleveland-Cliffs plans $1B Middletown Works upgrade with $500M DoE grant
data.description:
Cleveland-Cliffs (CLF) up 8.1% in Friday's trading after saying the U.S. Department of Energy has established a framework for the company to finalize negotiations and implementation plans for its modernization project at the Middletown Works facility in Ohio, rescoping the previously awarded $500M DoE grant.

The optimization project represents a $1B total investment in Middletown Works, with funding shared equally between the DoE and the company.

The proposal includes construction of a cogeneration plant and upgrades to a blast furnace and related material-handling operations.

Cleveland-Cliffs (CLF) said the investment is expected to begin in the coming weeks and be deployed over the next four years as it executes improvements while maintaining uninterrupted steel production, with completion of the blast furnace rebuild planned for Q1 2030.

Cleveland-Cliffs (CLF) is "making a decisive investment in the future of American steelmaking and manufacturing, going above and beyond a standard blast furnace reline," Chairman and CEO Lourenco Goncalves said. "The DoE's support for this project is a testament to the importance of preserving the blast furnace route to produce automotive-exposed grade steels in the U.S. while advancing American energy dominance."

data.title: Phillips 66 and Valero lead S&P energy holdings with 'A' growth grades
data.description:
As we navigate the third quarter of 2026, the S&P Energy sector continues to experience significant macroeconomic headwinds and shifting demand dynamics, making strategic stock selection and growth assessments a primary focus for active market participants.

Below is a list of the top holdings of the S&P Energy sector arranged according to their growth grade. These specific companies are selected because they represent the largest, most influential holdings in the sector by market capitalization, offering a comprehensive look at how the sector's heavyweights are scaling and expanding. Stocks with a grade of B- or above are considered Buys, while those with D+ or below fall into Sell territory.

The list is topped by Phillips 66 (PSX) and Valero Energy Corporation (VLO), both earning an A growth grade along with Strong Buy quant ratings. Marathon Petroleum Corporation (MPC) follows closely with an A- grade and also carries a Strong Buy rating.

The Williams Companies, Inc. (WMB) rounds out the Buy-rated stocks with a B+ growth grade, though it holds only a Hold quant rating. The remaining holdings, ConocoPhillips (COP), Chevron Corporation (CVX), ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation (XOM), EOG Resources, Inc. (EOG), Kinder Morgan, Inc. (KMI), and SLB N.V. (SLB), fall into the Hold or Sell tiers based on their growth grades ranging from C+ down to D-.

The growth factor grade is a quantitative assessment used in stock analysis to evaluate a company's growth prospects and expansion trajectory. This metric systematically analyzes multiple growth-related indicators to determine how effectively a company is scaling its business operations.

Growth factor grades are typically expressed on a letter scale (A+ through F), where higher grades indicate stronger growth characteristics relative to sector peers. An A+ grade represents exceptional growth potential, while lower grades suggest more moderate expansion or potential headwinds.

Here is the list:

  1. Phillips 66 (PSX), Growth grade: A

  2. Valero Energy Corporation (VLO), Growth grade: A

  3. Marathon Petroleum Corporation (MPC), Growth grade: A-

  4. The Williams Companies, Inc. (WMB), Growth grade: B+

  5. ConocoPhillips (COP), Growth grade: C+

  6. Chevron Corporation (CVX), Growth grade: C+

  7. ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation (XOM), Growth grade: C-

  8. EOG Resources, Inc. (EOG), Growth grade: D+

data.title: Nvidia receives 'top pick' as BMO initiates coverage on array of semiconductor stocks
data.description:
BMO initiated coverage on a range of semiconductor and quantum computing stocks on Thursday, with Nvidia (NVDA) receiving the "top pick" among the group due to its full-stack combination of hardware and software and its dominance in market share.

Nvidia received a $340 price target along with an Outperform rating.

"Next-gen Vera Rubin NVL72 system ramps in 2H," wrote analyst Harsh Kumar in an exhaustive investor report. Stock trades at an 18x forward P/E, a discount considering revenue growth of 84% and 50% in FY27 and FY28, respectively, based on our model. We believe market valuations are mispricing an opportunity given a defensible full systems end-to-end HW/SW moat."

BMO was bullish over several AI-exposed semi stocks, including Broadcom (AVGO), AMD (AMD), Marvell (MRVL) and Semtech (SMTC). These all received Outperform ratings with targets of $455, $550, $250 and $155, respectively.

"We see AVGO as the #2 AI supplier led by custom ASIC (XPU) and networking," Kumar noted. "The AAPL supply agreement has been renewed, while infra software remains mission-critical for enterprises. AMD's Helios joins the full rack market, primed with three lead customers (OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic). MRVL is a top optical PAM4 supplier and is gaining momentum in XPU/XPU-attach and switches. STMC's revenues incrementally step up from ACC/LPO connectivity."

In the analog space, BMO handed out Outperform ratings to Analog Devices (ADI), Impinj (PI) and Microchip Technology (MCHP). They received price targets of $430, $220 and $95, respectively.

"Analog names are emerging from post-COVID correction," Kumar said. "We're seeing positive signals supporting growth in analog. PMI >50, excess channel inventory cleared, book-to-bill above 1, bookings/backlogs starting to grow, and customer expedites are picking up. Industry was the first to recover, while auto showing positive signs. Defense is also solid from geo tensions."

Among quantum, D-Wave (QBTS) earned an Outperform rating and a $35 price target. BMO views the company as one of the best suited for commercial success due to its presence in two leading quantum approaches.
